summary:
H.R. 8884, the “Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act,” amends title II of the Social Security Act to temporarily reauthorize and modify the Social Security Administration’s authority to conduct disability insurance demonstration projects under section 234 (42 U.S.C. 434).

Section 2(a) amends the project termination date in section 234(d)(2) (42 U.S.C. 434(d)(2)) by striking the existing sunset of December 31, 2021, for initiating new projects and the corresponding carry-out termination date of December 31, 2022, and inserting new dates of December 31, 2030, and December 31, 2031, respectively.

Section 2(b) amends section 234(c) (42 U.S.C. 434(c)) in three respects: it extends the Commissioner’s authority to waive compliance with title II benefit requirements from December 30, 2021, to December 31, 2030; increases the advance notification period to Congress for such waivers from 90 days to 120 days; and adds a requirement that the Commissioner’s report to Congress include “evaluation metrics to be used with respect to the experiment or demonstration project.”

Section 2(c) amends section 201(k) (42 U.S.C. 401(k)) in its entirety to provide that administrative expenditures for section 234 projects shall be paid from funds made available for the administration of title II, while benefits paid to participants shall be made from the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund or the Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund, as the Commissioner determines appropriate.

Section 2(d) adds a new paragraph (4) to the limitations in section 234(e) (42 U.S.C. 434(e)), prohibiting any experiment or demonstration project from reducing an individual’s total income due to participation.

Section 2(e) makes two technical amendments to section 234: it corrects a cross-reference in subsection (d)(1) by replacing “subsection” with “section,” and it strikes subsection (f) in its entirety, thereby repealing a prior limitation on the number of demonstration projects.

The amendments made by section 2 take effect on January 1, 2027. The bill contains no new appropriation; it solely clarifies the source of funds and reauthorizes demonstration authority with modified conditions.
